questions.question: Which de-identification technique still allows re-identification using separately stored information?
questions.explanation: Pseudonymization maps identifiers to codes whose key is kept apart, so the link to the individual can be restored — unlike irreversible anonymization.

questions.question: Which principle requires collecting only the personal data necessary for the stated purpose?
questions.explanation: Data minimization limits collection to what is adequate and necessary — gathering excess data 'just in case' violates it.

questions.question: Which principle restricts processing to the specific purpose disclosed to the data subject?
questions.explanation: Purpose limitation binds use of the data to the purpose declared at collection; unrelated secondary uses need a new lawful basis.

questions.question: Which principle requires deleting or anonymizing personal data once it is no longer needed?
questions.explanation: Storage limitation caps retention at what is necessary for the declared purpose, after which data must be securely disposed of or anonymized.

questions.question: Processing personal data to comply with a statute falls under which GDPR lawful basis?
questions.explanation: Processing necessary to comply with the law — such as tax or court-ordered disclosures — rests on the legal obligation basis, needing no consent.

questions.question: What role must an organization designate to be accountable for DPA compliance?
questions.explanation: The Data Protection Officer monitors compliance, advises on obligations, and liaises with the NPC; designation is mandatory for covered organizations.

questions.question: Within how many hours must a qualifying personal data breach be reported to the NPC?
questions.explanation: NPC rules require notification of the Commission and affected data subjects within 72 hours of knowledge of a qualifying breach.

questions.question: Which data subject right allows correcting inaccurate or incomplete personal data?
questions.explanation: The right to rectification entitles data subjects to have inaccurate personal data corrected and incomplete data completed.

questions.question: Which right lets a user obtain their data in a structured format to move it to another provider?
questions.explanation: Data portability requires controllers to provide data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format transferable to another controller.

questions.question: The 'right to be forgotten' is formally known as what?
questions.explanation: The right to erasure lets data subjects demand deletion of their personal data when, for example, it is no longer necessary or consent is withdrawn.

questions.question: What document informs users how their personal data is collected, used, and shared?
questions.explanation: A privacy notice (or policy) satisfies the transparency principle by describing what data is collected, why, and with whom it is shared.

questions.question: Which DPA principle requires processing to be adequate, relevant, suitable, and not excessive?
questions.explanation: The Philippine DPA's three principles are transparency, legitimate purpose, and proportionality — the last limits processing to what the purpose demands.

questions.question: What formal agreement governs personal data shared between two separate controllers?
questions.explanation: A data sharing agreement documents the parties' obligations, security measures, and data subject rights when personal data is disclosed between controllers.

questions.question: What assessment systematically evaluates a project's risks to personal data privacy before launch?
questions.explanation: A Privacy Impact Assessment (called a DPIA under GDPR) identifies and mitigates privacy risks in a system or program before it goes live.

questions.question: What technique replaces real personal data with altered but realistic values in test environments?
questions.explanation: Data masking substitutes production personal data with fictitious values so developers and testers never handle real data subjects' information.
